alabama.name: Alabama
alabama.alt: Map of Alabama colored by median mid-greendown week, 2001 to 2017, from the USA National Phenology Network. The legend runs from Sept 1–7 through Oct 6–12. Darker red is an earlier week and gold to olive is later. Tan areas are not assigned a fall-color week.
alabama.caption: Color bands on this map of Alabama are seven-day groups of the median mid-greendown day for 2001–2017, from the USA National Phenology Network. Mid-greendown is the day satellite greenness last fell halfway from its annual peak, which that network uses as a metric of autumn leaf-color change. The legend lists Sept 1–7 through Oct 6–12. Cells before September 1, and cells with no reading, are left tan and are not given a fall-color week. Weeks with fewer than 0.5 percent of the colored cells stay on the map in their own color and are left off the legend. This is not a ranger forecast for this year.
alabama.sourceTitle: USA National Phenology Network, Land Surface Phenology 2001–2017
alabama.outlineSourceTitle: U.S. Census Bureau cartographic boundary files

alaska.name: Alaska
alaska.alt: Outline map of Alaska. Peak-week color bands are not shown because the 2001–2017 mid-greendown grid does not cover it.
alaska.caption: Outline only. The USA National Phenology Network mid-greendown grid covers the contiguous United States and has no cells in Alaska, so peak-week bands are not drawn. The regional window already stated on this page: Arctic and Interior mid-August to mid-September. Southcentral in September. Inside Passage late September into early October.
alaska.sourceTitle: USA National Phenology Network, Land Surface Phenology 2001–2017
alaska.outlineSourceTitle: U.S. Census Bureau cartographic boundary files

oregon.caption: Color bands on this map of Oregon are seven-day groups of the median mid-greendown day for 2001–2017, from the USA National Phenology Network. Mid-greendown is the day satellite greenness last fell halfway from its annual peak, which that network uses as a metric of autumn leaf-color change. The legend lists Sept 1–7 through Nov 10–16. Cells before September 1, and cells with no reading, are left tan and are not given a fall-color week. Weeks with fewer than 0.5 percent of the colored cells stay on the map in their own color and are left off the legend. This is not a ranger forecast for this year.
oregon.sourceTitle: USA National Phenology Network, Land Surface Phenology 2001–2017
oregon.outlineSourceTitle: U.S. Census Bureau cartographic boundary files
